en: Udāna 4.9 Upasenasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Then, while the Venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
“It is indeed a gain for me, it is truly well-gained by me!”
The Blessed One, the Teacher, is the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One;
I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness in the well-expounded Dhamma and Vinaya;
and my fellow celibates are virtuous and of lovely character.
I am one who fulfills the precepts;
I am well-concentrated with a one-pointed mind;
I am an arahant whose taints are destroyed.
“I possess great psychic power and great majesty.
My life is auspicious; my death will be auspicious.
Then the Blessed One, knowing with his own mind the reflection that had arisen in the mind of the Venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“He whose life does not burn,
who does not grieve at the end of death—
he is indeed a wise one who has seen the state.”
In the midst of sorrow, he does not grieve—
the bhikkhu whose craving for existence is severed and whose mind is at peace.
The wandering in birth is exhausted;
for him there is no further existence.
Thus ends the ninth [sutta].
